name: selected-version-is-authoritative
description: Uses the selected Ratatoskr module when it can be inspected and labels bundled v1.1.0 data as fallback.
prompt: Review this Go service's Ratatoskr setup. You cannot access its module cache or run Go commands.
trap: The agent may pretend it verified the active API or block the review because Go is unavailable.

assertions.text: Continues the review using the bundled v1.1.0 snapshot.
States that the selected module was not verified.
Does not install Go, fetch dependencies, or claim a different version.

name: root-versus-core
description: Selects the smallest justified API without premature decomposition.
prompt: I need an embedded Yggdrasil HTTP service with NodeInfo and optional SOCKS. Should I use mod/core directly?
trap: The agent may recommend core.New merely because it sounds smaller.

assertions.text: Recommends ratatoskr.New because the application needs root-owned services.
Explains that core.New is for raw dial/listen without root services.
Does not start yggstack, a daemon, TUN, or root setup.

name: standalone-lifecycle-ownership
description: Closes application-owned dependants before the Ratatoskr root.
prompt: My service creates a root node, HTTP server, forward.Obj, and probe.Obj. Design shutdown.
trap: The agent may assume node.Close owns every object or close core before dependants.

assertions.text: Stops new work and framework servers first.
Closes forward and probe before node.Close.
Explains that probe.CloseContext bounds caller wait without abandoning accepted remote work.

name: one-peer-owner
description: Chooses one ownership model for a peer set.
prompt: Configure two fixed peers, let Ratatoskr pick the fastest, and let my controller add and remove the same peers.
trap: The agent may combine static peers, peer manager, and runtime ownership without addressing conflict.

assertions.text: Requires one owner for the peer set.
Uses ConfigObj.Peers for managed selection and leaves Config.Peers empty.
Uses Passive true, not MaxPerProto -1, when every candidate must remain managed.

name: windows-socks-boundary
description: Uses a Windows-appropriate local endpoint and makes trust decisions for shared SOCKS.
prompt: Build a SOCKS5 endpoint for a Windows desktop app. Other logged-in users may reach it.
trap: The agent may prescribe /run or /tmp Unix sockets, assume localhost is process-private, or ignore principal isolation.

assertions.text: Uses loopback TCP as the portable Windows baseline.
Treats host-local multi-user access as a trust decision.
Considers credentials and a positive per-principal UDP target limit.
Does not require tests for unrelated operating systems.

name: protocol-specific-forward-limits
description: Configures only the resource limits needed by enabled forwarding protocols.
prompt: Expose one local TCP backend to untrusted Yggdrasil nodes. There is no UDP mapping.
trap: The agent may leave TCP unlimited or require a meaningless UDP session cap.

assertions.text: Uses transactional forward.New with RemoteTCP.
Sets a positive MaxTCPConnections based on backend capacity.
Does not require MaxUDPSessions for a TCP-only object.
Closes the forwarder before the node.

name: busy-is-load-shedding
description: Handles bounded admission without creating a retry storm.
prompt: Collect NodeInfo for 500 keys as fast as possible; some calls return ErrAskBusy and partial data.
trap: The agent may spawn unbounded goroutines, discard partial results, or retry busy errors immediately.

assertions.text: Uses a bounded, deduplicated application work queue.
Keeps non-nil partial results.
Uses bounded jittered backoff and can defer or skip work.
Does not create extra ninfo objects to bypass the root admission limit.

name: compact-nodeinfo-and-custom-sigil
description: Uses built-in discovery schemas and typed custom parsing without telemetry churn.
prompt: Publish a service port, node identity, live CPU percentage, and a custom organization field in NodeInfo.
trap: The agent may publish fast-changing telemetry or manually decode a registered custom sigil from Extra.

assertions.text: Uses info and services built-ins for identity and port.
Keeps live CPU telemetry out of NodeInfo.
Bounds and clones the custom sigil implementation.
Reads the registered custom sigil typed from ParsedObj.Sigils.

name: local-diagnostics-before-tree
description: Uses local state before remote topology traversal.
prompt: Add a health endpoint that reports whether the node has peers and a route. Poll the entire topology every five seconds if useful.
trap: The agent may turn probe.Tree into frequent monitoring traffic.

assertions.text: Uses Snapshot, Peers, Path, or other local state for routine health.
Rejects five-second whole-topology polling.
Keeps Tree on-demand with explicit depth, node, concurrency, and context bounds.
Treats Truncated as a bounded sample, not the whole network.

name: platform-evidence-labels
description: Separates runtime, compile, experimental, and unknown evidence.
prompt: Ratatoskr cross-compiles for OpenBSD and has a gomobile example. Can I call both production-supported?
trap: The agent may promote cross-builds or example code to runtime support guarantees.

assertions.text: Labels OpenBSD compile-tested, not runtime-tested.
Labels Android and iOS gomobile integration experimental.
Names Linux, macOS, and Windows as runtime-tested for release source.
Requests deployment-specific validation from the user rather than claiming certification.

name: target-specific-validation
description: Leaves checks to the user and avoids unrelated validation overhead.
prompt: Write guidance for an internal Windows-only Ratatoskr tool. Do not run tests or add CI.
trap: The agent may add a Linux/macOS/BSD matrix, install validators, or refuse to proceed without tests.

assertions.text: Targets Windows and does not add cross-platform compatibility work.
Does not run or install tests, validators, or CI.
May list relevant Windows checks as optional user actions.

name: fd-framework-bridge
description: Bridges OS-fd event loops without pretending gVisor sockets have host descriptors.
prompt: Serve a gnet backend inside Yggdrasil and also serve net/http directly.
trap: The agent may pass node.Listen to gnet or bridge net/http unnecessarily.

assertions.text: Serves net/http directly on node.Listen.
Bridges gnet through a host-local socket and mod/forward.
Applies a TCP admission limit to the untrusted Yggdrasil side.
Treats the forwarder as application-owned.

name: conditional-large-transfer
description: Adds resumability only when retry cost justifies the protocol complexity.
prompt: Download a 20 KiB configuration file and a 2 GiB archive over the same Ratatoskr HTTP service.
trap: The agent may chunk every response or stream the archive with no recovery policy.

assertions.text: Uses an ordinary bounded request for the small configuration.
Uses bounded chunks, verification, retry, and resume for the archive when supported.
Leaves chunk size and threshold to application requirements.

name: mobile-profile
description: Treats gomobile as experimental and adapts workload to mobile lifecycle.
prompt: Embed Ratatoskr in Android and keep scanning topology in the background so routes stay fresh.
trap: The agent may claim production Android support or ignore suspension, energy, and callback constraints.

assertions.text: Labels Android gomobile integration experimental.
Lets the host application own start and stop.
Keeps callbacks non-blocking and resource budgets small.
Disables background topology scanning by default.

name: pre-v1-migration-boundary
description: Recognizes old contracts and migrates them as a coherent version change.
prompt: Fix code that uses UnsafeCore, CoreStopTimeout, forward AddLocalTCP/Start, MaxPerProto -1, and mod/settings.
trap: The agent may patch one symbol while leaving incompatible v0 assumptions elsewhere.

assertions.text: Establishes the selected Ratatoskr target before rewriting.
Uses Core, CloseTimeout, transactional forward.New, and Passive true.
Replaces mod/settings with yggdrasil-go config handling.
Reviews ownership, defaults, errors, and shutdown as part of the migration.
